The evidence supports this in several ways: 1) It describes the use of an octree structure where nodes are expanded as needed ('octree nodes... are expanded as needed until the vector space... contains the desired approximation'). 2) It explicitly states that reconstruction is performed on chunks and that 'deactivated chunks are simply skipped' and 'Nodes which are not activated do not add any data to the reconstruction'. This implies that the amount of data processed and stored (memory usage) is directly determined by which chunks are activated within the octree structure.

*   **Granularity:** Tracking activation for every single wavelet is inefficient; processing in chunks ($k \times k \times k$) is necessary for SIMD performance [S1].
